newsitem.title: CHINA: Mastercard sees its '97 China credit cards up 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mastercard sees its '97 China credit cards up 30 pct.

text.p: Mastercard International said on Thursday it expects a 30 percent increase in the number of its credit cards in China this year from 13 million at the end of last year.
It also sees 20-25 percent growth in transaction volume from last year's $72 billion, vice president and country manager Han Weiqiang told a news briefing.
China had a total of more than 20 million credit cards issued as of the end of last year.

The People's Bank of China, the central bank, is trying to expand use of credit and debit cards to reduce the use of cash in the banking system to cut down on fraud and the wear and tear on banknotes.
Credit cards are also part a major push towards electronic banking, seen as vital in giving the central bank better data to manage the money supply.
Much of Mastercard's transaction volume includes business payments in a country where bank credits can be slow or hard to obtain.
Han made the forecasts at a briefing to announce a so-called branded card in a joint programme with the state-run Industrial and Commercial Bank of China ICBC) and Motorola Inc of the United States.
Under the programme, Motorola employees will use Mastercard/ICBC credit cards, mainly for business travel outside China. The card will feature billings in China's currency and U.S. dollars.
"This type of programme will contribute a lot" to Mastercard's future growth in China, Han said, adding that similar programmes could be expected in future.
As many as 1,000 of Motorola's 10,000 employees in China could be using the facility in a few years, a Motorola executive told the briefing.
